newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says wants no interpretive leeway on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says wants no interpretive leeway on EMU.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday that Germany would not tolerate a softening of the Maastricht criteria for the single European currency.
"We will not be party to an interpretive softening of the convergence criteria or to budgetary sleight-of-hand," Waigel told a meeting of this Christian Social Union political party.
Meeting the criteria must take priority over the timeplan for European economic and monetary union, due to start on January 1, 1999, Waigel said.
Those who call for a delay in the process risk causing a flight to the mark in financial markets, he said.

Germany must make a show of force to meet the criteria, he said. Recent political agreemeents would bring the country's public sector deficit to 99 billion marks, or 2.5 percent of gross domestic product, well below the 3.0 percent target prescribed by the Maastricht Treaty, he said.
